about: CHAIN saxon_exiles_804 (Design/content/CHAINS.md; page Design/content/chains/saxon_exiles_804.md; words Data/writing/chain_saxon_exiles_804.json). The last deportation of the Saxon war: in the summer of 804 the emperor moves every Saxon of Wihmodia and beyond the Elbe into Francia with wives and children and gives the land beyond the Elbe to the Obodrites (Annales regni Francorum 804; Einhard, Vita Karoli c. 7). One family of Wihmodia has reached the Ems mouth and wants passage; the count's men watch the rivers; and a people remembers who helped. Fourteen cards, 804 to about 811. The spine's thread saxon_end: its flag sx_carried_fugitive is set here where its meaning is met. Step flags ch_saxon_exiles_804_1 .. _10; state flags _hired, _bread, _kept, _turned_away, _took, _to_priest, _told, _watched, _bought_time, _taken, _hidden, _surety, _spoke, _exodus_plan, _run, _exodus_done, _exodus_half, _redeemed, _letter, _bant; waits are flags that run out (_wait_north, _wait_end, _wait_church, _wait_given). Endings: ch_saxon_exiles_804_end_north (what happened to those who fled: with the hard road, history changed: changed_wihmodia_exodus), ch_saxon_exiles_804_end_given (what happened to most), ch_saxon_exiles_804_end_church, ch_saxon_exiles_804_end_home (history changed: changed_wihmodia_resettled), ch_saxon_exiles_804_end_terp. Every ending also sets ch_saxon_exiles_804_done. Every option's note names its outcome text. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, one of two ways in (drawn at Diusburg, Colonia or Daventre from the summer of 804 to the end of 805). The deported come down to the Rhine on foot under guard and an officer wants hulls. Sources: Annales regni Francorum 804 (all the Saxons beyond the Elbe and in Wihmodia moved into Francia with women and children); Einhard, Vita Karoli c. 7 (ten thousand, settled in many groups through Gaul and Germany); chronicle_793.json 804-summer-nordalbingia-emptied; the spine's hooks for Diusburg and Colonia. That boats were hired for them is the spine's placing (?). The officer is an ordinary invented man, unnamed. Sets ch_saxon_exiles_804_1.

cards.note: Step 2, the other way in and the heart of it (scheduled by step 1; also drawn at Emuthon from the summer of 804 to the end of 805 by anyone). A family of Wihmodia, eleven nights through the marsh, lies hidden in the sheep house on the terp (places/emuthon.json emuthon.sheep_house) and wants passage to the father's brother among the Danes. Sources: Annales regni Francorum 804, which also say that the emperor sent an embassy to Godfred about the return of fugitives, so Saxons did flee to the Danes that summer; Widukind fled to the Danes in 777 and 782 (ARF). The Ems mouth as their road is the game's placing (?): Wihmodia lies between the lower Weser and the Elbe, and Rustringen and the Jade lie between it and Emuthon. Cast: Tetta the host is places/emuthon.json emuthon.tetta. Meginward, Aldburg his wife, Ricswind his mother, Folcward the boy and Gerburg the girl are ordinary invented people (Old Saxon name parts Megin-, -ward, Ald-, -burg, Ric-, -swind, Folc-, Ger-). The danger is told before it comes: the host names the guard boat at the river mouth. Sets ch_saxon_exiles_804_2 and either _took (with the spine's sx_carried_fugitive) or _kept.

cards.note: Step 3 (scheduled by step 2 or by turning back in step 4; drawn at Emuthon while the family is kept there). The count's man reads out the order at the toll post (places/emuthon.json emuthon.toll_post). Sources: the order of 804 as step 1; Emuthon is the king's own place in the district Emisga (dossiers/emuthon.md); no officer there is named in any source, so Gundhart is invented (Frankish Gund- + -hart). The reward for a finder and the penalty for a carrier are the game's (?): no capitulary on hiding the deported survives; the half share to the finder is borrowed from Thionville 805 c. 7 on arms. Sets ch_saxon_exiles_804_3; telling sets _told and leads to the ending end_given.

cards.note: Step 4 (drawn under way while the five are aboard). The count's men who watch the rivers: a guard boat hails. Sources: Einhard, Vita Karoli c. 17 (a fleet built against the Northmen and watches set at the harbours and the mouths of the rivers, from about 800); chronicle_793.json 802-spring-coast-ships-802. That such a watch was used to stop fugitives is the game's reading (?). The danger was told in step 2 and step 5. A failure costs a fine and the passengers, who go into the column; the story then goes on by the bishop's road (step 9). Sets ch_saxon_exiles_804_4.

cards.note: Step 5 (scheduled by step 3 or 4; drawn at Emuthon while the family is kept there and has not been given up). The host cannot keep them: three roads. North to the Danes; up the river to Liudger, who is priest and teacher of these districts and of the western Saxons at Mimigernaford (Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.22-23) and can ask for them in the open; or hidden as Frisians on the outer terp. Sources: Bant, the island district of Liudger's mission (Altfrid I.22), is now a sandbank (dossiers/emuthon.md); hiding Saxons as Frisians is invented, and rests on the two tongues being half understood by each other (npc_text_encounters.md 2.6). Cast: emuthon.tetta, cast.liudger named. Sets ch_saxon_exiles_804_5 and _took (with _to_priest for the river road) or _hidden.

cards.note: Step 6 (drawn on the first call at Ripa or Sliesthorp with the five aboard). A stranger among the Danes has no peace unless a man of the place stands for him; Meginfrid, the brother, is away. Sources: Annales regni Francorum 804 (Godfred with his fleet and all the horsemen of his kingdom at Sliesthorp, on the border of his realm and Saxony); the guest's need of a host among the Northmen is in Rimbert, Vita Anskarii c. 24-27 (merchants under a king's or a chief's peace) and in Hávamál's opening stanzas; a lawman at Ripa is invented (?). Meginfrid is invented (Megin- + -frid). Sets ch_saxon_exiles_804_6 and a wait of thirty days.

cards.note: Step 7, the turn (drawn at Ripa or Sliesthorp a month after step 6). The king's spokesman asks the Frisian what he saw; Meginfrid pays his brother's passage. Sources: Annales regni Francorum 804: Godfred promised to come to a meeting with the emperor and did not, kept back by the counsel of his men; the emperor sat at Hollenstedt on the Elbe and sent an embassy to him about the return of fugitives (pro perfugis reddendis). What Godfred answered is not recorded; the game lets him keep them, as nothing says they were returned (?). Godfred speaks to merchants through a spokesman (spine: cast.godfred, who is named and not met). The hard road opens here: Meginward's kin, forty people, still lie in the reeds by the Jade (invented). Sets ch_saxon_exiles_804_7 and a wait, or _exodus_plan.

cards.note: Step 8, the hard road (scheduled by step 7; drawn at Emuthon). Forty of Meginward's kin on a reed island at the edge of the Jade, and a boat that holds five. Sources: the Gislinge boat's load (BRIEF.md); the pilot Folcger is places/emuthon.json emuthon.folcger; the Jade and the Weser mouth were open tidal marsh with channels only local men knew (dossiers/emuthon.md on the Ems flats; the Jade by likeness (?)). Sets ch_saxon_exiles_804_run and _exodus_done or _exodus_half.

cards.note: Step 9, the lawful road (drawn at Daventre or Diusburg with the five aboard, or after they were taken from the boat; scheduled by a failure in step 4). Liudger asks for them. Sources: Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.22-24: teacher of the Frisian districts from 787 and of the western Saxons at Mimigernaford, founder of Werden on the Ruhr about 799, bishop from 30 March 805, died 26 March 809; the deported were set down in groups on royal and church land (Einhard c. 7), so a bishop asking for one family for his own house's land is within the order and not against it, though no such case is recorded (?); ransoming captives as a good work (reputation_793.json bought_captives, gave_alms); the Old Saxon baptismal vow (texts_793.json saxon_vow), which the spine has a priest read to the deported again. Cast: cast.liudger (places: daventre, diusburg). Sets ch_saxon_exiles_804_9, a wait of sixty days, and _redeemed, _letter or _surety.

cards.note: Step 10, the turn of the long road (drawn at Emuthon from 806 to 809 while the family lives hidden as Frisians). The count's man comes back with a list. Sources: lists of Saxons by name were kept: the Indiculus obsidum Saxonum Moguntiam deducendorum of about 805 names 37 hostages and their keepers (MGH Capitularia I no. 115) (?); a list of the missing of Wihmodia is invented. An oath with oath-helpers clears a man in Frisian law (Lex Frisionum, passim). Bant as step 5. The boy Folcward, fourteen now, comes aboard as a hand; Aldburg and Ricswind have woven three bolts in two winters (the weaver's trade at Emuthon: places/emuthon.json emuthon.imma). Sets ch_saxon_exiles_804_10.

cards.note: ENDING end_north (drawn at Ripa or Sliesthorp when the wait after step 7 or 8 has run out). The ones who went north: what happened to the Saxons who fled to the Danes in 804, of whom nothing more is written. With the hard road done it is history changed (changed_wihmodia_exodus): forty-five people of one kin get out together and keep their name and law among the Danes. Sources as steps 6 to 8; guest right and a booth place at a Danish market (Rimbert, Vita Anskarii c. 24: the king gives a place for a church and leave to trade at Sliaswic, by likeness); the felag, a sworn partnership, is named on later rune stones (CHAINS.md) (?) for 804. Grand rewards: unlock_title_danish_guest_right; with the forty, also unlock_partner_meginfrid; or unlock_plot_ripa. Lasting cost: ch_saxon_exiles_804_watched, if set, stays (the count's men know the boat). Sets ch_saxon_exiles_804_end_north and ch_saxon_exiles_804_done.

cards.note: ENDING end_church (drawn at Daventre or Diusburg sixty days after step 9). The lawful road: the five are the Church's people on Werden's land on the Ruhr, a day above Diusburg, inside the emperor's order. Not recorded of any family, and not against anything recorded (?). Sources: Werden founded by Liudger about 799 on his own land (Altfrid I.21 (?) for the chapter; the oldest Werden charters, from 793, are land gifts on the Ruhr and the lower Rhine); abbeys kept men at river landings to see to their trade (the toll freedoms of Saint-Germain and Saint-Denis; Werden's own later rights at Diusburg (?)). Wax and honey are what a Saxon holding paid its church. Grand rewards: unlock_title_lords_protection (the bishop's), unlock_factor_diusburg (Meginward keeps the abbey's landing and your goods); both, if the merchant paid the price himself. Sets ch_saxon_exiles_804_end_church and ch_saxon_exiles_804_done.

cards.note: ENDINGS end_home and end_terp (drawn at Emuthon from 810, after step 10). HISTORY CHANGED (changed_wihmodia_resettled): in the record the people of Wihmodia are scattered through Gaul and Germany and are not heard of again as a people; here one hamlet is lived in again by the people who left it. Sources: Annales regni Francorum 808-811: Godfred falls on the Obodrites (808), the Franks take the north back and build Esesfeld on the Stor (begun 15 March 809), Godfred's two hundred ships take a hundred pounds of silver from the Frisians and he is killed (810), peace is sworn on the Eider by twelve men of each side (811); that the deported were then allowed home is a modern guess for the land beyond the Elbe ('vermutlich', de.wikipedia Nordalbingien, read 6 Oct 2026) and Louis the Pious is said to have given Saxons and Frisians back the right to their fathers' land in 814 (the Astronomer, Vita Hludowici c. 24) (?). Silver buried before a flight is the common reason for a hoard (npc_text_encounters.md 1.5; hoards_793.json). Grand rewards: unlock_pilot_weser (the gullies of the Jade and the Weser mouth), unlock_heirloom_weser_arm_ring (with the hard option), or unlock_factor_emuthon if they stay Frisians (ending end_terp, history not changed). Sets ch_saxon_exiles_804_end_home or ch_saxon_exiles_804_end_terp, and ch_saxon_exiles_804_done.

cards.title: The empty land
cards.intention: Six winters a Frisian shepherd, Meginward has heard what every shipman is saying: the Wends have lost the north, the emperor's counts are building on the far side of the Elbe, and nobody is counting heads on the Weser marsh any more.
